bullets: CRL duel game 2 vs Lava Hound / Rune Giant / Valkyrie beatdown, video t=2250-2454 (broadcast clock unreadable). Ryley wins it to level the set at 1-1: "I was able to take the tower guys. So we were going to a game three" (t=2448).

Gameplan is permanent pressure so the beatdown player can never bank for a Hound: five Royal Hogs bridge deploys (t=2257, 2292, 2346 split, 2391, 2415) plus Dark Prince at the bridge (t=2320, 2367, 2437) and Barbarian Barrel + Goblins at the bridge (t=2370, 2424) — "I was just constantly spamming him because I don't want to let him get many lava hound pushes" (t=2351).

Furnace and Goblin Hut are cycled as a pair, seven Furnace placements between t=2256 and t=2420, so a single opponent spell can never clear both: "since he had to waste his evo zap, he was unable to take out my furnace or my goblin hut cuz obviously I was going to cycle back to a new set of goblin hut and furnace" (t=2404).

The Evo Royal Hogs threat is what protects the spawners: "I was just kind of abusing the fact that he couldn't really spell my furnace away because he had to watch out for the evo piggies" (t=2342); when the opponent is pinned defending hogs, the Furnace moves up to the river so its Fire Spirits cross the bridge (t=2420).

Defence is Dark Prince + spawner chip, played on prediction rather than reaction — a pre-placed Dark Prince at [9, 11] (t=2393) against a Valkyrie that had not yet been shown — and the game closes with the Heroic Dark Prince dismount plus Fireball (t=2441-2448).

new_deck.rationale: No tank and no big spell win condition: every card is a cheap threat dropped at the bridge (Royal Hogs, Dark Prince, Barbarian Barrel, Goblins) to force answers, with the two huts holding the ground behind it.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Two spawners (Furnace and Goblin Hut) generate free chip and free defenders, so the deck can defend a Lava Hound push with elixir left over and immediately spend it at the bridge. Royal Hogs are the pressure valve rather than the whole plan — the threat of the Evolution in cycle stops the opponent from spending a spell on the huts, and stops them committing to a Hound at all. Dark Prince covers the ground defence that the huts cannot (Valkyrie, Barbarians) and doubles as a bridge threat, with the Heroic Destructive Dismount available when the opponent is already stretched. Fireball is both the defensive answer to Skeleton Dragons and the finisher, since two Fireballs is a real win condition once the hut chip has worked. The weakness on show is air defence: the one Hound push that did get through took a tower from full to ~1720.
